paragraphs.english: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage. In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems. These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
paragraphs.chinese: 过去，美国顾客通常会给那些他们认为主要靠小费获取收入的人付小费，例如工资低于最低工资标准的餐厅服务员。2010年代初，许多不同类型的商家开始使用iPad和其他数字支付系统处理交易。这些系统常常提示顾客，为过去通常不用给小费的服务支付小费。

paragraphs.english: Today’s tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip. Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered. That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
paragraphs.chinese: 如今，商家索要小费时，往往已经与过去决定人们何时给、怎样给小费的工资和服务惯例脱节。过去，顾客几乎总是在接受服务后才给小费，例如吃完一顿饭、理完发，或披萨送达后。这样的支付时机能够奖励优质服务，并激励工作人员提供优质服务。

paragraphs.english: It’s becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand. And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
paragraphs.chinese: 提前索要小费变得越来越普遍。而新的小费支付技术，甚至可能自动把小费加进账单。

paragraphs.english: The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip. That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services. Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options — often well above 20% of what they owe. The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today. This increase is sometimes called tipflation — the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
paragraphs.chinese: 数字支付设备的普及，让商家更容易向顾客索要小费。这有助于解释，为什么小费要求正在渗入新的服务类型。现在，顾客经常会看到一组预设的建议小费选项，往往远高于应付款项的20%。小费比例从20世纪50年代的10%或更低，上升到2000年前后的15%，再到如今的20%甚至更高。这种增长有时被称为“小费通胀”，也就是小费金额被期待不断上涨。

paragraphs.english: Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US $2.13 an hour. Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
paragraphs.chinese: 在餐饮等传统上收取小费的服务行业里，小费一直是员工的重要收入来源；这些行业适用于小费员工的最低工资，可能低至每小时2.13美元。如今，小费适用范围的扩张和小费通胀，又进一步增加了许多低薪服务人员的收入。

paragraphs.english: Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers. To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement towards no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
paragraphs.chinese: 值得注意的是，小费主要使这些员工中的一部分人受益，例如服务员，却不能同样惠及厨师和洗碗工等其他员工。为了让所有员工都获得公平工资，一些餐厅禁止收小费，并提高价格，但这种转向无小费服务的运动大多已逐渐消退。

paragraphs.english: So to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to temptations of tip creep and tipflation. However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip too often. And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous, and often completely dissociated from service quality.
paragraphs.chinese: 因此，为了不提高价格又能增加员工工资，越来越多雇主开始抵挡不住扩大小费适用范围和提高小费金额的诱惑。不过，许多顾客感到沮丧，因为他们觉得自己被索要过高小费的频率太高了。而且，正如我们的研究所强调的，如今的小费似乎更像被迫支付，较少体现自愿慷慨，并且常常与服务质量完全脱节。

sentenceNotes.sentence: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
sentenceNotes.structure: people后省略关系代词，they assumed为嵌入成分，可理解为“他们认为靠小费谋生的人”；such as举例；earning分词短语修饰restaurant servers。
sentenceNotes.translation: 过去，美国顾客通常会给那些他们认为主要靠小费获取收入的人付小费，例如工资低于最低工资标准的餐厅服务员。
sentenceNotes.tip: 不要把they assumed当作新主句；它说明顾客如何判断收小费者的收入来源。

sentenceNotes.sentence: To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement towards no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement ... has largely fizzled out.
sentenceNotes.structure: 句首不定式表目的，that从句是ensure的宾语；banned与increased并列；but转折指出这项改革的最终发展情况。
sentenceNotes.translation: 为了让所有员工都获得公平工资，一些餐厅禁止收小费，并提高价格，但这种转向无小费服务的运动大多已逐渐消退。
sentenceNotes.tip: fizzle out指逐渐失去势头而消退；先分清改革目的，再看转折后的现实结果。
